description: AI provider model-training defaults relevant to skill authors. Point-in-time facts with sources and verification method. STALE entries (older than 60 days without re-verification) must be rendered with their date, never as current fact.

providers.surface: Claude consumer plans (Free, Pro, Max), including Claude Code sessions on those plans
providers.training_default: user-choice toggle; existing-user acceptance dialog shipped with the toggle pre-set to on (functionally opt-out)
providers.toggle: Privacy settings: model training / improvement setting (consumer terms announced 2025-08-28; existing-user acceptance deadline 2025-10-08, earlier acceptance effective immediately)
providers.retention: 5 years if training is allowed; 30 days if not

providers.surface: Commercial: API, Team, Enterprise, API-billed Claude Code, third-party platforms
providers.training_default: no training on customer content by default; opt-in only via explicit programs (e.g. Development Partner Program)
content used for model training by default
providers.toggle: Settings > Data Controls > 'Improve the model for everyone' (off = opt out)
providers.retention: standard retention; a litigation preservation order affected deletion timing during 2025 (ended 2025-09-26 per OpenAI), not the training default
providers.note: OpenAI pages block automated fetchers; entry corroborated via multiple independent secondary sources. Re-verify manually in a browser before relying on wording.

providers.training_default: separate in-product data controls, including a training toggle covering code and full environments
providers.toggle: Codex settings: 'Do not use code for AI training' (location per current Codex UI)
providers.note: Verify in the Codex app; control names change.

providers.surface: Business: API, ChatGPT Business/Team, Enterprise, Edu

legal_context.item: EU: DSM Directive Art 4(3) machine-readable TDM rights reservation; EU AI Act Art 53(1)(c) (in force 2025-08-02) requires GPAI providers to honour such reservations including for training outside the EU. Which formats qualify is pending European Commission guidance (consultation closed 2026-01-23, after an extension).

US: Bartz v. Anthropic (N.D. Cal. 2025) held training on lawfully acquired books to be fair use; the enforceability of a machine-readable reservation against a lawful acquirer was not adjudicated. Settlement final approval 2026-07-20.
